title: I Took the Hospital Volunteer Badge Log to the Charge Who Borrowed Mine

parts.text: I signed in at 6:48 a.m. and my volunteer badge was already on the charge nurse's lanyard. The badge log she initialed said: ONE BADGE PER PERSON. NO LENDING. I was twenty-two, wayfinding volunteer, holding a paper backup that did not open doors. Charge Nia said, "I needed a reader for a cart." I pointed at the log. She clipped mine tighter. "Charges are the floor." I photographed the lanyard, the log, and my empty clip. Then I took the stills to security with the sign-in sheet. At 6:54 security asked why Nia's name was on a badge-lend ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Security can see my volunteer badge on the charge lanyard against her no-lending log.

social.video_title: The charge clipped my volunteer badge — Part 1/2
social.description: Empty clip, a cart excuse, and a log she initialed. I walked it to security. Would you have wayfound with paper?

parts.text: Nia called it a minute until security pulled the door reads. I printed the ticket, the log, and the photo. My badge came back. Nia used her own reader and told the station the log was always about optics. Optics is a word charges use when a door log exists. Volunteer policy now has a second line: CARTS ARE NOT VOLUNTEERS. I clip in. Nia badges in. The doors finally know who opened them.

social.video_title: Carts are not volunteer badges — Part 2/2
social.description: Door reads, a returned clip, and a second line on the log. Was a minute ever a lanyard?
